biophysical_burden.boundary: Global average population-index decline cited by the assessment; not the share of species extinct or the condition of every water body.

human_economic_burden.non_addition_rule: Score the larger source population envelope only because the two basin populations may overlap.

extent.boundary: Country share with at least one degraded water-related ecosystem type.

source_locators: UN-Water 2024 update: one or more water-related ecosystem types are degraded in 50 percent of countries, more than 90 of 185 reporting countries.
UN-Water 2024 report: freshwater species populations have declined globally by 83 percent since 1970.
UN-Water 2024 update: river flow significantly decreased in 402 of 12,572 basins, a fivefold increase from 15 years earlier, with 107.5 million people living in those basins.
UN-Water 2024 update: permanent surface water receded in 364 of 13,894 basins, where 93.1 million people live.
excluded_from_scoring: the sum of potentially overlapping reduced-flow and receding-water populations
unreported ecosystems treated as stable or degraded

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-cited global freshwater species-population decline and the larger non-additive exposed-population envelope through named ranges.
Use the 1970-2024 report interval without extrapolating the decline.
Use the source-reported 50 percent of countries with at least one degraded water-related ecosystem type; do not interpret this as all ecosystems in those countries.

receipts.uncertainty: Country reporting, satellite coverage, basin delineation, trend significance, observation epochs, monitoring density and national indicator composition vary. A country is counted degraded when at least one included ecosystem type is degraded; this does not mean every freshwater ecosystem in that country is degraded.
receipts.freshness: UNEP and UN-Water SDG 6.6.1 assessment 2024; snapshot captured 2026-07-31T21:47:06.642Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: UNEP and UN-Water quantify global freshwater species-population decline, human exposure in reduced-flow basins, multi-decade persistence and country-level degradation extent.
higher_priority_failures: The operational EPA survey is a bounded 2018-2019 conterminous-US river and stream estimate and cannot supply a current global freshwater aggregation or 20-year global history.

biophysical_burden.boundary: Significant decreased-flow basin inventory; no cause is assigned.

human_economic_burden.boundary: Population residing in affected basins; not a count of people experiencing a measured household impact.

transformations.formula: Normalize the source-reported fivefold increase in significantly decreased-flow basins relative to 15 years earlier.
Normalize the source-reported population living in reduced-flow basins through a named global range.
Divide significantly decreased-flow basins by all assessed river basins; never treat unassessed basins as unaffected.
